title: The w-record law is width-based dynamic programming
claim: The w-record law (carry joint records of up to w distinctions; absorb, forget, combine) decides and counts not-all-equal patterns exactly when w >= treewidth + 1 (pathwidth + 1 without combining): bucket elimination (known). NAE seam reports are the complement-closed relations, 2^(2^(s-1)) of them; two-place shadows determine all at s <= 2 and 12 of 16 at s = 3, the 4 failures being NAE and its single-flip variants, all knots; at s = 4, 50 and 226 of 256 are fixed by two- and three-place shadows (computed). Escapes from width are known: affine records, Pfaffians, Petersen on the sphere.
standard_statement: Tree-decomposition dynamic programming for Boolean CSP; complement-closed relations as the co-clone of NAE; k-decomposability of relations.
prior_work: Freuder 1990; Dechter and Pearl 1989; Dechter 1999; Samer and Szeider 2010; Aji and McEliece 2000; Elberfeld, Jakoby and Tantau 2010; Bodlaender and Hagerup 1998; Marx 2010; Baker and Pixley 1975; Jeavons, Cohen and Cooper 1998; Moret 1988; Hadlock 1975; Kasteleyn; Valiant.
